states.changed: The work exists: one Globe at Night report at a time, its night sky set for its place and minute goes out faintest star first down to what the observer saw, with a lens that restores the sky and a band of twenty years of reports.

A re-timed report now turns from the hour it was filed at, its constellation under the ground, to its local hour; the band's new bottom rows open the reports no sky can be given (drawn as star trails of every possible hour, or as an outline over 0°N 0°E); and a visitor can go out themselves, take their own sky down to what they see, and file it in the band's last column.
